# Genres and tags

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:genres` from packages/core/src/composer (genres.ts, styles.ts, tag-catalog.ts). Do not edit by hand. -->

Song Deck ships **57 genre profiles** — full rule sets for tempo, meter, modes, harmony, form, instrumentation, groove, dynamics and production that can be blended ("50% pop-punk / 30% emo / 20% cinematic") — and **487 tags** that nudge a blend without being a full profile: 297 style, 63 mood, 13 era, 31 production, 24 vocal, 34 region, 25 rhythm.

A style tag names parent genres: picked on its own it pulls the blend toward them ("midwest emo" → emo + indie rock); added to a blend it reshapes the profile (tempo window, groove, harmony, line-up, production). Mood, era, production, vocal, region and rhythm tags only reshape. Tag macro changes are applied at generation time on top of the song's own macros.

## Genres

### Pop (`pop`)

Hook-centred songwriting with clear verse/chorus contrast and polished, punchy production.

- **Tempo:** 88–132 BPM (typically 112) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** major 65%, minor 35%
- **Harmony:** `I V vi IV`, `vi IV I V`, `I vi IV V` · extensions 20% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `pop` drums, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Verse / Pre / Chorus; Verse / Chorus; Verse / Pre / Chorus / Post-chorus
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Drum Kit, Electric Bass, Piano (often with Clean Electric Guitar, Synth Pad)
- **Sound:** Polished modern pop: punchy drums, bright upfront vocals, wide pads

### Synth-Pop (`synth-pop`)

Synth-driven pop with steady electronic grooves, arpeggios and lush pads.

- **Tempo:** 100–135 BPM (typically 118) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 55%, major 45%
- **Harmony:** `vi IV I V`, `i VI III VII`, `I V vi IV` · extensions 25% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `synth-pop` drums, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Verse / Pre / Chorus; Verse / Pre / Chorus / Post-chorus; Verse / Chorus
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Electronic Drum Kit, Synth Bass, Synth Pad (often with Synth Arp, Synth Lead)
- **Sound:** Glossy synth-pop: gated drums, analog-style synths, chorus-drenched pads

### Punk (`punk`)

Fast, raw and loud: power chords, driving eighths and short songs.

- **Tempo:** 150–210 BPM (typically 178) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** major 55%, minor 45%
- **Harmony:** `I IV V IV`, `I V vi IV`, `I bVII IV I` · extensions 0% · 1 chord(s)/bar · power chords
- **Groove:** `punk` drums, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Punk (verse / chorus); Punk (long verses)
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Drum Kit, Electric Bass, Distorted Guitar (often with Distorted Guitar)
- **Sound:** Raw garage punk: loud guitars, crashy drums, shouted vocals

- **Harmony:** `I V vi IV`, `vi IV I V`, `IV I V vi` · extensions 5% · 1 chord(s)/bar · power chords
- **Groove:** `pop-punk` drums, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Rock anthem; Punk (verse / chorus); Verse / Pre / Chorus
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Drum Kit, Electric Bass, Distorted Guitar, Distorted Guitar (often with Lead Guitar)
- **Sound:** Tight, bright pop-punk: double-tracked guitars, punchy kick, big singalong vocals

### Emo (`emo`)

- **Sound:** K-pop: hyper-polished maximal production, genre-switching sections, dance break, layered group vocals

### J-Pop (`j-pop`)

Japanese pop and anime songs: fast chord changes, the "royal road" progression, A-melo/B-melo/sabi forms, last-chorus key lift.

- **Tempo:** 100–184 BPM (typically 140) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** major 55%, minor 45%
- **Harmony:** `IVmaj7 V7 iii7 vi`, `vi IV V I`, `IV V iii vi` · extensions 45% · 2 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `pop` drums, 16th grid
- **Forms:** J-pop (A-melo / B-melo / sabi); Verse / Pre / Chorus / Post-chorus
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Drum Kit, Electric Bass (often with Distorted Guitar, Piano, String Ensemble)
- **Sound:** J-pop: bright busy arrangements, fast chord changes, melodic bass, sparkling keys, dramatic last-chorus lift

### Drum and Bass (`drum-and-bass`)

Breakbeats at 170+ BPM over half-speed reese sub-bass and atmospheric pads.

- **Tempo:** 165–178 BPM (typically 174) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 80%, dorian 20%
- **Harmony:** `i VI III VII`, `i7 iv7`, `i VII VI VII` · extensions 50% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `drum-and-bass` drums, `kick-lock` bass, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Drum and bass (two drops); EDM (instrumental)
- **Band:** Electronic Drum Kit, Synth Bass, Synth Pad (often with Synth Lead)
- **Sound:** Drum and bass: fast chopped breaks, growling reese sub-bass, atmospheric pads, rolling energy

### Dubstep (`dubstep`)

Half-time 140 BPM bass music: kick on 1, snare on 3, wobbling and growling bass drops.

- **Tempo:** 136–150 BPM (typically 140) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 60%, phrygian 25%, harmonic-minor 15%
- **Harmony:** `i VI`, `i bII`, `i iv VI V` · extensions 10% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `dubstep` drums, `wobble` bass, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Dubstep (two drops); EDM (vocal, two drops)
- **Band:** Electronic Drum Kit, Synth Bass (often with Synth Lead, Synth Pad)
- **Sound:** Dubstep: half-time drums, massive wobble and growl bass, sub drops, dark atmospherics

### Techno (`techno`)

Hypnotic, minimal four-on-the-floor machine music: rumbling kicks, off-beat hats, evolving sequences.

- **Tempo:** 124–142 BPM (typically 130) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 60%, phrygian 20%, dorian 20%
- **Harmony:** `i7`, `i VII`, `i iv` · extensions 30% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `techno` drums, `offbeat` bass, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Techno (DJ-friendly); EDM (instrumental)
- **Band:** Electronic Drum Kit, Synth Bass, Synth Sequence (often with Synth Pad, Synth Arp, Percussion)
- **Sound:** Techno: relentless four-on-the-floor, hypnotic sequences, rumbling kick, industrial textures, long builds

### Ambient (`ambient`)

Slow-evolving, atmospheric music: sustained pads, long reverbs, sparse piano and little or no rhythm.

- **Tempo:** 56–100 BPM (typically 70) · **Meter:** 4/4 70%, 3/4 15%, 6/8 15%
- **Modes:** major 40%, lydian 20%, minor 25%, dorian 15%
- **Harmony:** `Imaj7 IVmaj7`, `Iadd9 IVadd9`, `vi7 IVmaj7` · extensions 70% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `ambient` drums, `sustain` bass, `arpeggio` comping, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Ambient (slow movements); Cinematic (two builds)
- **Band:** Synth Pad, Piano (often with String Ensemble, Synth Arp)
- **Sound:** Ambient: slow-evolving pads, long reverb tails, sparse piano, gentle textures, no hard transients

### Lo-Fi Hip-Hop (`lo-fi-hip-hop`)

Dusty, swung boom-bap beats under warm Rhodes and jazzy seventh chords — chill study music.

- **Tempo:** 68–92 BPM (typically 80) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 45%, dorian 25%, major 30%
- **Harmony:** `ii7 V7 Imaj7 vi7`, `IVmaj7 iii7 vi7`, `i7 iv7` · extensions 90% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `boom-bap` drums, swing 45%, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Lo-fi loop; Hip-hop (16-bar verses)
- **Band:** Drum Kit, Electric Piano, Electric Bass
- **Sound:** Lo-fi hip-hop: dusty swung drums, warm Rhodes, jazzy chords, tape hiss and vinyl crackle, soft sidechain

### Trap (`trap`)

Atlanta-born hip-hop: rattling hi-hat rolls, booming 808s, half-time snares and dark minimal loops.

- **Tempo:** 128–160 BPM (typically 140) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 70%, phrygian 15%, harmonic-minor 15%
- **Harmony:** `i VI`, `i iv`, `i VI III VII` · extensions 20% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `trap` drums, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Hook first (16-bar verses); Hip-hop (16-bar verses)
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Electronic Drum Kit, 808 Bass (often with Piano, Synth Pad)
- **Sound:** Trap: rattling hi-hat rolls, booming 808s, crisp snares, dark minimal melodies

### Drill (`drill`)

UK / Brooklyn drill: sliding 808s, syncopated half-time drums, cold piano and string melodies.

- **Tempo:** 136–148 BPM (typically 142) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 55%, harmonic-minor 30%, phrygian 15%
- **Harmony:** `i VI`, `i VI iv V`, `i bII` · extensions 10% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `drill` drums, `eight-o-eight` bass, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Hook first (16-bar verses); Hip-hop (16-bar verses)
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Electronic Drum Kit, 808 Bass (often with Piano, String Ensemble)
- **Sound:** UK / NY drill: sliding 808s, syncopated half-time drums, cold piano and string melodies

### Grunge (`grunge`)

Sludgy, fuzzed-out 90s rock: quiet verses, explosive choruses, chromatic power-chord riffs.

- **Tempo:** 80–140 BPM (typically 108) · **Meter:** 4/4 90%, 6/8 10%
- **Modes:** minor 60%, mixolydian 20%, dorian 20%
- **Harmony:** `i III iv VI`, `I bIII IV`, `I bVI bVII I` · extensions 5% · 1 chord(s)/bar · power chords
- **Groove:** `rock` drums, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Emo (breakdown before the last chorus); Rock anthem
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Drum Kit, Electric Bass, Distorted Guitar (often with Distorted Guitar)
- **Sound:** Grunge: sludgy fuzz guitars, loose heavy drums, quiet-verse/loud-chorus dynamics, raw vocals

### Shoegaze (`shoegaze`)

Walls of reverb-drenched fuzz guitar, buried dreamy vocals, washing cymbals and slow-moving harmony.

- **Tempo:** 88–142 BPM (typically 118) · **Meter:** 4/4 90%, 3/4 10%
- **Modes:** major 50%, minor 30%, lydian 20%
- **Harmony:** `I bVII IV`, `I iii IV iv`, `vi IV I V` · extensions 40% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `indie` drums, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Indie (interlude); Rock anthem
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Drum Kit, Electric Bass, Distorted Guitar (often with Distorted Guitar, Synth Pad)
- **Sound:** Shoegaze: walls of reverb-drenched fuzz guitars, buried dreamy vocals, washing cymbals

### Post-Rock (`post-rock`)

Instrumental rock built on long crescendos: delay-soaked guitar arpeggios swelling into towering climaxes.

- **Tempo:** 70–140 BPM (typically 110) · **Meter:** 4/4 80%, 3/4 10%, 6/8 10%
- **Modes:** minor 50%, major 35%, lydian 15%
- **Harmony:** `vi IV I V`, `i VI III VII`, `I IV vi V` · extensions 30% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `rock` drums, `arpeggio` comping, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Post-rock (crescendo); Cinematic (two builds)
- **Band:** Drum Kit, Electric Bass, Clean Electric Guitar (often with Distorted Guitar, Clean Electric Guitar, String Ensemble)
- **Sound:** Post-rock: instrumental crescendos, delay-soaked guitars, swelling strings, climactic walls of sound

### Bluegrass (`bluegrass`)

Appalachian string band at full gallop: banjo rolls, mandolin chop, fiddle breaks, boom-chick guitar, high lonesome harmony.

- **Tempo:** 120–240 BPM (typically 184) · **Meter:** 4/4 85%, 3/4 15%
- **Modes:** major 85%, mixolydian 10%, minor 5%
- **Harmony:** `I IV I V`, `I IV V I`, `IV I V I` · extensions 5% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `country` drums, `root-fifth` bass, swing 8%, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Bluegrass (instrumental breaks); Country (solo)
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Banjo, Acoustic Guitar, Mandolin, Upright Bass (often with Violin, Backing Vocals)
- **Sound:** Bluegrass: acoustic string band around one mic: banjo rolls, mandolin chop, fiddle breaks, upright bass, high harmonies

### Synthwave (`synthwave`)

Retro 80s soundtrack nostalgia: driving eighth-note bass, gated snares, analog poly pads and soaring leads.

- **Tempo:** 80–120 BPM (typically 100) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 75%, dorian 10%, major 15%
- **Harmony:** `i VI III VII`, `VI VII i i`, `i VII VI VII` · extensions 20% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `synth-pop` drums, `eighths` bass, `sustain` comping, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Synthwave (lead solo); Verse / Chorus
- **Band:** Electronic Drum Kit, Synth Bass, Synth Pad (often with Synth Lead, Synth Arp)
- **Sound:** Synthwave: gated-reverb snares, analog poly synths, driving eighth-note bass, neon 80s nostalgia

### Phonk (`phonk`)

Memphis-rap-rooted beats: cowbell melodies, distorted 808s, half-time trap drums and lo-fi grit.

- **Tempo:** 120–150 BPM (typically 132) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 55%, phrygian 30%, harmonic-minor 15%
- **Harmony:** `i VI`, `i bII`, `i iv` · extensions 10% · 0.5 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `phonk` drums, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Hook first (16-bar verses); Hip-hop (16-bar verses)
- **Band:** Electronic Drum Kit, 808 Bass (often with Synth Lead, Lead Vocal)
- **Sound:** Phonk: cowbell melodies, distorted 808s, Memphis-rap vocal chops, lo-fi tape grit

### Hyperpop (`hyperpop`)

Maximalist, glitchy internet pop: pitched-up vocals, blown-out 808s, sugary synths and abrupt switch-ups.

- **Tempo:** 120–172 BPM (typically 150) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** major 55%, minor 45%
- **Harmony:** `I V vi IV`, `IV V iii vi`, `vi IV I V` · extensions 30% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `trap` drums, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Hyperpop (glitch drop); Verse / Chorus
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Electronic Drum Kit, 808 Bass (often with Synth Lead, Synth Arp, Synth Pad)
- **Sound:** Hyperpop: maximalist, distorted and glitchy; pitched-up vocals, blown-out 808s, sugary synths

### UK Garage (`uk-garage`)

Skippy, shuffled 2-step drums, warm sub-bass, M1-style organ stabs and chopped soulful vocals.

- **Tempo:** 128–138 BPM (typically 132) · **Meter:** 4/4 100%
- **Modes:** minor 60%, dorian 25%, major 15%
- **Harmony:** `i7 iv7`, `IVmaj7 iii7 vi7`, `ii7 V7 Imaj7 vi7` · extensions 80% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `two-step` drums, `stabs` comping, swing 35%, 16th grid
- **Forms:** UK garage; House
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Electronic Drum Kit, Synth Bass (often with Organ, Synth Pad)
- **Sound:** UK garage: skippy shuffled 2-step drums, warm sub bass, organ stabs, chopped soulful vocals

### Singer-Songwriter (`singer-songwriter`)

Intimate, lyric-first songs for one voice and a guitar or piano, with minimal accompaniment.

- **Tempo:** 64–122 BPM (typically 88) · **Meter:** 4/4 75%, 3/4 15%, 6/8 10%
- **Modes:** major 60%, minor 40%
- **Harmony:** `I V vi IV`, `vi IV I V`, `IV I V vi` · extensions 25% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `folk` drums, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Verse / Chorus; Folk (three verses)
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Acoustic Guitar (often with Piano)
- **Sound:** Singer-songwriter: intimate close-miked voice and guitar or piano, minimal accompaniment

### Musical Theatre (`musical-theatre`)

Broadway show tunes: piano-led pit orchestra, storytelling verses, belted choruses and a key-change finale.

- **Tempo:** 70–152 BPM (typically 108) · **Meter:** 4/4 70%, 3/4 20%, 6/8 10%
- **Modes:** major 65%, minor 35%
- **Harmony:** `I vi ii V`, `I iii IV V`, `IV V I vi` · extensions 40% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `pop` drums, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Show tune (key-change finale); Verse / Pre / Chorus
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Piano (often with String Ensemble, Contrabass, Drum Kit, Brass Section)
- **Sound:** Musical theatre: Broadway pit orchestra, piano-led, belted storytelling vocals, big final key change

### Chiptune (`chiptune`)

Video-game music in the style of 8-bit consoles: pulse-wave leads, rapid arpeggios, octave bass and noise drums.

- **Tempo:** 118–182 BPM (typically 150) · **Meter:** 4/4 90%, 3/4 10%
- **Modes:** major 55%, minor 45%
- **Harmony:** `I V vi IV`, `i VI VII i`, `I IV V IV` · extensions 10% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `synth-pop` drums, `octave` bass, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Video game loop (stages and boss)
- **Band:** Chiptune Lead, Synth Bass, Synth Arp, Electronic Drum Kit
- **Sound:** Chiptune / video game music: square and pulse waves, fast arpeggios, noise-channel drums, 8-bit console limits

### Flamenco (`flamenco`)

Andalusian guitar music: the Andalusian cadence, fiery rasgueado strums, palmas and cajón, passionate cante.

- **Tempo:** 90–140 BPM (typically 112) · **Meter:** 4/4 60%, 3/4 25%, 6/8 15%
- **Modes:** minor 50%, harmonic-minor 30%, phrygian 20%
- **Harmony:** `i VII VI V`, `i iv V i`, `I bII I` · extensions 10% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `flamenco` drums, `root-fifth` bass, `rasgueado` comping, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Flamenco / rumba (falsetas); Folk (three verses)
- **Band:** Nylon Guitar, Lead Vocal, Percussion (often with Drum Kit, Nylon Guitar)
- **Sound:** Flamenco / rumba: fiery nylon-guitar rasgueados and falsetas, palmas, cajón, passionate cante

### Celtic (`celtic`)

Irish and Scottish folk: fiddle and whistle tunes in AABB form, lilting jigs and reels, bodhrán and strummed guitar.

- **Tempo:** 88–180 BPM (typically 116) · **Meter:** 4/4 50%, 6/8 35%, 3/4 15%
- **Modes:** major 45%, mixolydian 25%, dorian 20%, minor 10%
- **Harmony:** `I IV I V`, `i VII i VII`, `I IV V I` · extensions 5% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `celtic` drums, swing 15%, 8th grid
- **Forms:** Celtic tune set (AABB); Folk (three verses)
- **Band:** Violin, Acoustic Guitar (often with Flute, Percussion, Lead Vocal)
- **Sound:** Celtic folk: fiddle and tin whistle melodies, bodhrán, strummed guitar/bouzouki, lilting rhythm

### Bollywood (`bollywood`)

Hindi film songs (filmi): lush strings, dhol and tabla grooves, sitar and bansuri hooks, soaring playback vocals.

- **Tempo:** 80–132 BPM (typically 105) · **Meter:** 4/4 85%, 6/8 15%
- **Modes:** minor 45%, harmonic-minor 25%, major 30%
- **Harmony:** `i iv V i`, `i VI VII i`, `i VII VI V` · extensions 15% · 1 chord(s)/bar
- **Groove:** `bhangra` drums, swing 35%, 16th grid
- **Forms:** Filmi song (mukhda / antara); Verse / Pre / Chorus
- **Band:** Lead Vocal, Drum Kit, Electric Bass (often with Percussion, String Ensemble, Sitar, Flute, Backing Vocals)
- **Sound:** Bollywood / filmi: lush film strings, dhol and tabla grooves, sitar and bansuri hooks, soaring playback vocals

## Style tags (microgenres)

### Rock & alternative

- **Post-punk** (`post-punk` → Punk, Indie Rock) — Angular guitars, a driving melodic bass up front and cold, roomy drums _Also: post punk, post-punk revival._
- **New wave** (`new-wave` → Synth-Pop, Rock) — Jittery late-70s/80s pop-rock: synths, chorus guitars, robotic eighths _Also: new-wave._
- **Darkwave** (`darkwave` → Synth-Pop, Indie Rock) — Cold minor-key drum machines, gothic synth pads and a baritone gloom _Also: coldwave, dark wave._
- **Gothic rock** (`gothic-rock` → Alternative Rock, Synth-Pop) — Brooding minor-key rock: tom-heavy grooves, flanged guitars, cavernous reverb _Also: goth rock, goth._
- **Garage rock** (`garage-rock` → Rock, Punk) — Raw, fast, fuzzy and a little sloppy: three chords and a cheap amp
- **Psychedelic rock** (`psychedelic-rock` → Rock, Indie Rock) — Modal drones, swirling organ, phased guitars and long jams _Also: psych rock, psychedelia, acid rock._
- **Stoner rock** (`stoner-rock` → Rock, Metal) — Slow, fuzzed-out, down-tuned riffs that lock into a heavy groove _Also: desert rock, stoner._
- **Surf rock** (`surf-rock` → Rock) — Reverb-soaked twangy lead guitar, galloping drums, minor-key drama _Also: surf._
- **Southern rock** (`southern-rock` → Rock, Country) — Bluesy, twin-guitar rock with a swagger and a country accent
- **Classic rock** (`classic-rock` → Rock) — 70s radio rock: riffs, Hammond organ, big drums and guitar solos
- **Hard rock** (`hard-rock` → Rock, Metal) — Loud, riff-first rock with swagger: crunchy guitars, big drums, belted vocals
- **Glam rock** (`glam-rock` → Rock, Pop) — Stomping, handclapped boogie rock with glitter and big singalong hooks _Also: glam._
- **Arena rock** (`arena-rock` → Rock, Pop) — Stadium-sized anthems: power ballads, big gated drums, keyboards and gang choruses _Also: stadium rock, aor._
- **Progressive rock** (`prog-rock` → Rock, Cinematic) — Long-form rock with odd meters, extended harmony, keyboard solos and suites _Also: prog, progressive rock._
- **Math rock** (`math-rock` → Indie Rock, Emo) — Intricate odd-meter riffs, tapped clean guitars and stop-start dynamics _Also: math-rock, mathrock._
- **Midwest emo** (`midwest-emo` → Emo, Indie Rock) — Twinkly interlocking clean guitars, maj7 shimmer, odd bars and confessional yelps _Also: twinkly emo, emo revival, twinkle emo._
- **Screamo** (`screamo` → Emo, Punk) — Frantic emo-hardcore: blast-fast sections, dissonant chords, screamed catharsis _Also: skramz._
- **Post-hardcore** (`post-hardcore` → Emo, Punk, Metal) — Hardcore energy with melodic hooks, clean/screamed contrast and dynamic builds
- **Britpop** (`britpop` → Indie Rock, Rock) — 90s British guitar pop: jangly-to-crunchy guitars, singalong choruses, swagger _Also: brit pop._
- **Noise rock** (`noise-rock` → Indie Rock, Punk) — Abrasive, dissonant guitars and pounding repetition
- **Slowcore** (`slowcore` → Indie Rock, Singer-Songwriter) — Glacial tempos, sparse clean guitars and hushed, heavy-hearted songs _Also: sadcore._
- **Krautrock** (`krautrock` → Indie Rock, Techno) — Hypnotic motorik beat, droning repetition and analog synth textures _Also: motorik rock, kosmische._
- **Space rock** (`space-rock` → Rock, Post-Rock) — Cosmic drones, delay-drenched guitars and swirling synths over a steady pulse
- **Blues rock** (`blues-rock` → Rock, Blues) — Overdriven blues licks, shuffles and pentatonic solos at rock volume
- **Rockabilly** (`rockabilly` → Rock, Country) — 50s rock and roll meets hillbilly boogie: slap upright bass, twangy leads, fast shuffle _Also: rock and roll, rock 'n' roll, rock n roll._
- **Power pop** (`power-pop` → Rock, Pop) — Crunchy guitars with Beatles-sweet melodies and stacked harmonies _Also: powerpop._
- **Yacht rock** (`yacht-rock` → Pop, Soul, Rock) — Smooth late-70s soft rock: Rhodes, maj7 chords, slick session grooves _Also: west coast aor, yacht._
- **Soft rock** (`soft-rock` → Rock, Pop) — Mellow, melodic rock with acoustic guitars, piano and warm harmonies _Also: mellow rock._
- **Heartland rock** (`heartland-rock` → Rock, Country) — Earnest American storytelling rock: driving eighths, organ, harmonica and big choruses _Also: heartland._
- **Post-grunge** (`post-grunge` → Grunge, Alternative Rock) — Radio-friendly heavy rock: drop-tuned crunch, polished production, big hooks
- **Dance-punk** (`dance-punk` → Punk, Disco) — Punk energy on a disco beat: cowbell, four-on-the-floor kick, wiry guitars _Also: dance punk, disco punk._
- **Blackgaze** (`blackgaze` → Shoegaze, Metal) — Black-metal blast beats under shoegaze walls of major-key shimmer
- **Alt-country** (`alt-country` → Country, Indie Rock) — Country songwriting with indie-rock grit: twangy guitars, ragged harmonies _Also: alt country, insurgent country._
- **Rap rock** (`rap-rock` → Rock, Hip-Hop) — Distorted riffs under rapped verses and shouted hooks _Also: rap metal._

### Metal

- **Nu metal** (`nu-metal` → Metal, Hip-Hop) — Drop-tuned groove riffs, hip-hop beats, turntable scratches and angst _Also: nu-metal, numetal._
- **Djent** (`djent` → Metal) — Palm-muted polyrhythmic chugs on extended-range guitars, ambient clean interludes
- **Sludge metal** (`sludge-metal` → Metal, Grunge) — Crushing, slow and filthy: down-tuned riffs, hardcore shouts, feedback _Also: sludge._
- **Doom metal** (`doom-metal` → Metal) — Funereal tempos, enormous minor riffs and mournful melodies _Also: doom._
- **Black metal** (`black-metal` → Metal) — Tremolo-picked minor chords, blast beats, cold lo-fi production, shrieked vocals
- **Death metal** (`death-metal` → Metal) — Brutal, chromatic riffing, blast beats and guttural growls _Also: death metal, deathmetal._
- **Thrash metal** (`thrash-metal` → Metal, Punk) — Fast palm-muted gallops, shouted gang choruses and shredding solos _Also: thrash, speed metal._
- **Power metal** (`power-metal` → Metal, Cinematic) — Galloping double-kick, soaring operatic melodies, harmonized leads and choirs
- **Symphonic metal** (`symphonic-metal` → Metal, Cinematic) — Metal band plus orchestra and choir: bombastic, cinematic, operatic
- **Metalcore** (`metalcore` → Metal, Emo) — Breakdowns, melodic choruses, screams versus cleans, palm-muted chugs
- **Deathcore** (`deathcore` → Metal) — Death-metal heaviness with slamming half-time breakdowns and low growls
- **Progressive metal** (`progressive-metal` → Metal) — Virtuosic, odd-metered metal epics with keyboard and guitar duels _Also: prog metal._
- **Glam metal** (`glam-metal` → Metal, Rock) — 80s hair metal: big hooks, flashy solos, gang choruses and power ballads _Also: hair metal._
- **Industrial metal** (`industrial-metal` → Metal, EDM) — Mechanical, sequenced metal: drum machines, samples, distorted synths and riffs _Also: industrial rock._
- **Folk metal** (`folk-metal` → Metal, Celtic) — Metal riffs carrying folk melodies on fiddle, whistle and accordion _Also: pagan metal, viking metal._
- **Post-metal** (`post-metal` → Metal, Post-Rock) — Slow-building, crushing crescendos of sludgy riffs and atmospheric swells _Also: atmospheric sludge._
- **Grindcore** (`grindcore` → Metal, Punk) — Ultra-fast blast beats and noisy micro-songs _Also: grind._
- **Trap metal** (`trap-metal` → Trap, Metal) — Screamed trap: distorted 808s, half-time drums and metal guitars _Also: scream rap._

### Punk & hardcore

- **Hardcore punk** (`hardcore-punk` → Punk) — Short, ferocious, ultra-fast songs with gang shouts and breakdown stomps _Also: hardcore, hxc, hc punk._
- **Skate punk** (`skate-punk` → Punk, Pop-Punk) — Fast, melodic, technically tight punk with soaring harmonized choruses _Also: skatepunk._
- **Melodic hardcore** (`melodic-hardcore` → Punk, Emo) — Hardcore urgency with minor-key melodies and emotional spoken/screamed builds
- **Street punk / Oi!** (`street-punk` → Punk) — Mid-tempo terrace chants, simple power chords and shouted gang choruses _Also: oi, oi!, street punk._
- **Ska-punk** (`ska-punk` → Ska, Punk) — Punk energy alternating with off-beat skank and horn lines _Also: ska punk, third wave ska._
- **Folk-punk** (`folk-punk` → Punk, Folk) — Acoustic guitars played punk-fast with ragged singalong vocals, banjo and fiddle _Also: folk punk._
- **Emo pop** (`emo-pop` → Pop-Punk, Emo) — Glossy pop-punk with emo heartbreak, synth touches and huge hooks _Also: emo-pop._
- **Easycore** (`easycore` → Pop-Punk, Metal) — Pop-punk choruses colliding with metalcore breakdowns _Also: pop-core._
- **Crust punk** (`crust-punk` → Punk, Metal) — Filthy, d-beat-driven punk with metallic riffs and political fury _Also: crust, d-beat._

### Pop

- **Bubblegum pop** (`bubblegum-pop` → Pop) — Sugary, simple, major-key earworms with handclaps and bright synths _Also: bubblegum, bubblegum bass._
- **Dance-pop** (`dance-pop` → Pop, EDM) — Club-ready pop: four-on-the-floor, sidechained synths and a big chorus drop _Also: dance pop, club pop._
- **Electropop** (`electropop` → Synth-Pop, Pop) — Pop built entirely from synths and drum machines: crisp, quirky, bright _Also: electro-pop, electro pop._
- **Teen pop** (`teen-pop` → Pop) — Y2K-style bright pop with tight harmonies, guitar-pop chords and big choruses
- **Art pop** (`art-pop` → Pop, Indie Rock) — Adventurous pop with unusual harmony, textures and arrangements _Also: avant-pop._
- **Power ballad** (`power-ballad` → Pop, Rock) — Slow-building ballad that explodes into a huge, belted final chorus _Also: ballad, big ballad._
- **Sophisti-pop** (`sophisti-pop` → Pop, Soul) — 80s jazz-tinged adult pop: sax, Rhodes, maj9 chords and smooth grooves
- **City pop** (`city-pop` → J-Pop, Funk, Disco) — 80s Tokyo urban pop: funky bass, glassy keys, maj7 chords and night-drive glamour _Also: citypop._
- **Girl-group pop** (`girl-group` → Pop, Soul) — 60s Wall-of-Sound girl groups: castanet-backbeat, strings, harmonized "ooh"s _Also: girl group._
- **Doo-wop** (`doo-wop` → Soul, Pop) — 50s vocal-group R&B in 12/8 over I–vi–IV–V with nonsense-syllable backing harmonies _Also: doowop, doo wop._
- **Adult contemporary** (`adult-contemporary` → Pop) — Smooth, mature, mid-tempo pop with piano and gentle grooves _Also: ac, easy listening._
- **Pop rock** (`pop-rock` → Pop, Rock) — Guitar-led pop with crunchy rhythm guitars and a radio chorus _Also: pop/rock._
- **Dark pop** (`dark-pop` → Pop, Trap) — Moody minor-key pop with sparse trap-influenced beats and breathy vocals _Also: alt-pop, alt pop._
- **K-ballad** (`k-ballad` → K-Pop, Pop) — Korean piano-and-strings ballad with an emotional key-lifted climax _Also: korean ballad, drama ost._
- **Mandopop / C-pop** (`mandopop` → Pop) — Chinese-language pop: pentatonic-tinged melodies, lush ballad arrangements _Also: c-pop, cpop, cantopop._
- **J-rock** (`j-rock` → J-Pop, Rock) — Japanese rock: fast melodic riffs, busy bass, dramatic anime-style choruses _Also: jrock, japanese rock._
- **Anime opening** (`anime` → J-Pop) — High-octane anime theme: fast tempo, dense chords, a dramatic key-lifted chorus _Also: anime, anime op, anime theme, anisong._
- **Vocaloid** (`vocaloid` → J-Pop, EDM) — Hyper-fast, dense J-pop with synthesized voice, glittering synths and rock drums _Also: miku, utaite._
- **Visual kei** (`visual-kei` → J-Pop, Metal) — Theatrical Japanese rock/metal: gothic drama, fast double-kick, symphonic keys
- **Shibuya-kei** (`shibuya-kei` → J-Pop, Bossa Nova) — Kitschy, sample-collage Japanese pop mixing bossa, lounge and 60s pop _Also: shibuya kei._
- **K-indie** (`k-indie` → K-Pop, Indie Rock) — Korean indie: intimate, jazzy-to-dreamy band pop with soft vocals _Also: korean indie._
- **Europop** (`europop` → Pop, EDM) — Bright, melodic continental pop with simple dance grooves and big sing-along hooks _Also: eurovision, euro pop._

### Indie

- **Bedroom pop** (`bedroom-pop` → Indie Rock, Pop) — Home-recorded, lo-fi pop: soft vocals, chorusy guitars, cheap drum machines _Also: bedroom-pop._
- **Dream pop** (`dream-pop` → Shoegaze, Indie Rock) — Hazy, reverb-washed pop: chorused guitars, breathy vocals, slow-motion grooves _Also: dreampop, dream-pop._
- **Jangle pop** (`jangle-pop` → Indie Rock, Pop) — Bright chiming 12-string-style clean guitars over sunny major chords _Also: jangle, jangly._
- **Indie pop** (`indie-pop` → Indie Rock, Pop) — Melodic, homespun pop with clean guitars, keys and earnest charm _Also: indiepop._
- **Twee pop** (`twee-pop` → Indie Rock, Pop) — Sweet, innocent indie pop with glockenspiel, handclaps and boy-girl vocals _Also: twee, c86._
- **Indie folk** (`indie-folk` → Folk, Indie Rock) — Fingerpicked acoustic guitars, stacked harmonies and swelling rustic arrangements _Also: indie-folk, stomp clap folk._
- **Chamber pop** (`chamber-pop` → Indie Rock, Orchestral, Pop) — Pop songs dressed in strings, woodwinds and piano with orchestral care
- **Baroque pop** (`baroque-pop` → Pop, Orchestral) — 60s-style pop with harpsichord-like keys, string quartets and descending basslines _Also: baroque rock._
- **Sunshine pop** (`sunshine-pop` → Pop, Indie Rock) — Late-60s California pop: lush harmonies, bright major chords, breezy grooves _Also: sunshine._
- **Freak folk** (`freak-folk` → Folk, Indie Rock) — Psychedelic, off-kilter acoustic music with drones and odd textures _Also: psych folk, psychedelic folk._

### House & techno

- **Deep house** (`deep-house` → House) — Warm, unhurried house: muted kicks, jazzy minor-ninth chords, soulful hums _Also: deep-house._
- **Tech house** (`tech-house` → House, Techno) — Minimal, percussive house with rolling basslines and groovy vocal chops _Also: tech-house._
- **Acid house** (`acid-house` → House, Techno) — Squelching TB-303-style resonant bassline over a jacking drum machine _Also: acid, 303, acid techno._
- **Progressive house** (`progressive-house` → House, Trance) — Long, melodic builds, evolving arps and emotional breakdowns _Also: prog house, melodic house._
- **Tropical house** (`tropical-house` → House, Pop) — Laid-back, sunny house at a slower tempo with marimba plucks and pan-flute leads _Also: trop house._
- **Afro house** (`afro-house` → House, Afrobeats) — House with African percussion, chanted vocals and hypnotic minor grooves _Also: afro-house, afro tech._
- **Electro house** (`electro-house` → House, EDM) — Big-room-leaning house with distorted, buzzy saw basslines _Also: electro-house, complextro._
- **Future house** (`future-house` → House, EDM) — Bouncy house with metallic, pitch-bent bass plucks and pop toplines
- **Chicago house** (`chicago-house` → House) — The original: jacking 909 drums, piano chords, diva vocals, raw and soulful _Also: piano house, jackin house._
- **French house** (`french-house` → House, Disco) — Filtered disco loops, phased pumping sidechain and funky guitar licks _Also: filter house, french touch._
- **Soulful house** (`soulful-house` → House, Gospel) — Gospel-tinged house with live keys, strings and powerhouse vocals _Also: gospel house, garage house._
- **Nu-disco** (`nu-disco` → Disco, House) — Modern disco revival: slick filtered grooves, octave bass and analog synths _Also: nu disco, disco house._
- **Minimal techno** (`minimal-techno` → Techno) — Stripped-back clicks and pulses: tiny variations over a hypnotic kick _Also: microhouse._
- **Detroit techno** (`detroit-techno` → Techno) — Soulful machine funk: 909 grooves, futuristic strings and minor-seventh pads
- **Industrial techno** (`industrial-techno` → Techno) — Distorted, pounding kicks, metallic percussion and harsh noise _Also: warehouse techno, hard techno._
- **Melodic techno** (`melodic-techno` → Techno, Trance) — Dark, emotive techno with arpeggiated leads and slow-moving minor chords
- **Dub techno** (`dub-techno` → Techno, Reggae) — Echoing minor chord stabs dissolving into reverb over a muffled kick
- **Psytrance** (`psytrance` → Trance, Techno) — Driving 140+ BPM trance with rolling 16th basslines and psychedelic phrygian leads _Also: psy trance, goa trance, goa, psy._
- **Uplifting trance** (`uplifting-trance` → Trance) — Euphoric supersaw anthems with long emotional breakdowns and key-lifted climaxes _Also: epic trance, vocal trance._
- **Hardstyle** (`hardstyle` → EDM, Trance) — Distorted reverse-bass kicks at 150 BPM with euphoric screeching leads _Also: rawstyle, hard dance._
- **Gabber / hardcore techno** (`gabber` → Techno, EDM) — Brutal 180+ BPM distorted kicks and rave stabs _Also: gabber, hardcore techno, frenchcore._
- **Big room** (`big-room` → EDM) — Festival EDM: huge minimal drops, snare-roll builds, simple anthemic leads _Also: bigroom, festival edm, mainstage._
- **Eurodance** (`eurodance` → EDM, Pop) — 90s Euro rave-pop: four-on-the-floor, rap verses, diva hooks and stabby synths _Also: euro dance, euro house, 90s dance._
- **Italo disco** (`italo-disco` → Disco, Synth-Pop) — 80s Italian synth-disco: octave basslines, vocoders and arpeggiated sequencers _Also: italo, italo-disco._
- **Hi-NRG** (`hi-nrg` → Disco, Synth-Pop) — Fast, high-energy 80s club music with relentless octave bass _Also: hi nrg._
- **Gqom** (`gqom` → House, Amapiano) — Durban's dark, broken-kick house: tribal toms, sparse and ominous
- **Kwaito** (`kwaito` → House, Amapiano, Hip-Hop) — Slowed-down South African house with chanted vocals and deep bass
- **Private school amapiano** (`private-school-piano` → Amapiano) — Jazzier, softer amapiano: lush piano, saxophone, gentle log drums _Also: private school, private school amapiano._

### Bass music & breaks

- **Future bass** (`future-bass` → EDM, Dubstep) — Half-time trap drums under huge detuned, pitch-bent supersaw chords _Also: future-bass, kawaii future bass._
- **Riddim** (`riddim` → Dubstep) — Minimal, repetitive, metallic dubstep bass hits with lots of space
- **Brostep** (`brostep` → Dubstep) — Aggressive mid-range growl basses and screeching drops _Also: tearout._
- **EDM trap** (`festival-trap` → EDM, Trap) — Festival trap: brass stabs, 808 drops, snare rolls and hype chants _Also: edm trap, trap edm._
- **Moombahton** (`moombahton` → Reggaetón, House) — House slowed to 108 BPM with a reggaetón dembow swing
- **Jersey club** (`jersey-club` → EDM, Hip-Hop) — Bouncy 140 BPM club music: five-kick bounce, bed-squeak samples, chopped vocals _Also: jersey._
- **Footwork** (`footwork` → Hip-Hop, EDM) — Chicago juke at 160: stuttering triplet kicks, chopped vocal loops, sparse 808s _Also: juke, chicago juke._
- **Grime** (`grime` → Drill, UK Garage) — London 140 BPM: cold square-wave basslines, eskibeat synths and rapid-fire MCs _Also: uk grime._
- **Speed garage** (`speed-garage` → UK Garage, House) — Pitched-up garage with four-on-the-floor kicks and warping "rubber" bass _Also: bassline, bassline house._
- **Future garage** (`future-garage` → UK Garage, Ambient) — Ghostly, reverb-soaked 2-step with pitched vocal snippets and vinyl hiss
- **Breaks** (`breakbeat` → EDM, Hip-Hop) — Chopped funk breakbeats driving rave stabs and bass _Also: breaks, nu skool breaks._
- **Big beat** (`big-beat` → EDM, Hip-Hop) — 90s block-rocking breakbeats, distorted riffs and sampled hooks
- **Jungle** (`jungle` → Drum and Bass, Reggae) — Frenetic chopped Amen breaks at 165+, ragga vocals and deep reggae sub-bass _Also: ragga jungle, oldschool jungle._
- **Liquid drum and bass** (`liquid-dnb` → Drum and Bass) — Smooth, melodic drum and bass with soulful pads, pianos and vocals _Also: liquid, liquid funk, liquid dnb._
- **Neurofunk** (`neurofunk` → Drum and Bass) — Technical, dark drum and bass with surgical, modulated reese basses _Also: neuro._
- **Jump-up** (`jump-up` → Drum and Bass) — Bouncy, cartoonish drum and bass with wobbling bass riffs built for the crowd _Also: jump up._
- **Breakcore** (`breakcore` → Drum and Bass, Hyperpop) — Chaotic hyper-chopped breakbeats at 180+ colliding with pretty melodies and noise
- **Baile funk** (`baile-funk` → Hip-Hop, Samba) — Rio's funk carioca: tamborzão drums, booming 808 hits and chanted MC hooks _Also: funk carioca, brazilian funk, funk brasileiro, mandelão._

### Synth & retro

- **Darksynth** (`darksynth` → Synthwave) — Aggressive, horror-tinged synthwave with distorted bass and metal energy _Also: dark synth, cyberpunk._
- **Chillwave** (`chillwave` → Synth-Pop, Ambient) — Hazy, nostalgic, lo-fi synth-pop with warped tape and summer haze _Also: glo-fi._
- **Vaporwave** (`vaporwave` → Synth-Pop, Ambient, Lo-Fi Hip-Hop) — Slowed, pitched-down 80s muzak and smooth-jazz samples drenched in reverb _Also: vapourwave, mallsoft._
- **Witch house** (`witch-house` → Trap, Ambient) — Occult, slowed trap beats with droning synths and ghostly pitched vocals _Also: witch-house._
- **Electro** (`electro` → EDM, Funk) — 808 electro-funk: robotic syncopated kicks, vocoders and laser synths _Also: electro funk, electro-funk._
- **EBM / industrial** (`ebm` → Synth-Pop, Techno) — Electronic body music: sequenced bass, marching drum machines, shouted vocals _Also: industrial, electronic body music._
- **Electroclash** (`electroclash` → Synth-Pop, Punk) — Deadpan punk attitude over cheap 80s drum machines and buzzing synths
- **Nightcore** (`nightcore` → EDM, Hyperpop) — Sped-up, pitched-up dance tracks with euphoric trance energy
- **Digicore** (`digicore` → Hyperpop, Trap) — Online-born pop-rap: glitchy, pitched-up, emo-melodic with hyperpop drums _Also: glitchcore._

### Downtempo & ambient

- **Trip-hop** (`trip-hop` → Hip-Hop, Ambient, Cinematic) — Slow, smoky breakbeats with dark jazz chords, strings and cinematic gloom _Also: trip hop, triphop, bristol sound._
- **Downtempo** (`downtempo` → Ambient, Hip-Hop) — Relaxed, groove-led electronica at walking pace _Also: down tempo._
- **Chillout** (`chillout` → Ambient, House) — Balearic sunset electronica: lush pads, guitars and slow grooves _Also: chill out, balearic, café del mar._
- **IDM** (`idm` → EDM, Ambient) — Intricate, glitchy electronic "listening" music with complex programmed rhythms _Also: intelligent dance music, glitch music._
- **Electronica** (`electronica` → EDM, Ambient) — Melodic, textural electronic music between club and home listening
- **Dark ambient** (`dark-ambient` → Ambient) — Ominous drones, sub rumbles and dissonant textures _Also: drone ambient._
- **Drone** (`drone` → Ambient) — Sustained tones and slowly shifting overtones with almost no harmonic movement
- **New age** (`new-age` → Ambient) — Gentle, consonant, meditative music with pads, piano, harp and flute _Also: meditation, healing music._
- **Lounge** (`lounge` → Jazz, Bossa Nova) — Cocktail-hour easy listening: brushed bossa grooves, vibraphone, smooth keys _Also: cocktail lounge, exotica._
- **Electro swing** (`electro-swing` → Jazz, House) — Vintage swing samples and horns on a house beat _Also: electroswing._
- **Nu jazz** (`nu-jazz` → Jazz, EDM) — Jazz harmony and improvisation over broken-beat and downtempo electronics _Also: jazztronica, broken beat._

### Hip-hop & rap

- **Boom bap** (`boom-bap` → Hip-Hop) — Hard-hitting sampled kicks and snares, swung 16ths, chopped soul and jazz loops _Also: boom-bap, boombap._
- **Golden age hip-hop** (`golden-age-hip-hop` → Hip-Hop, Funk) — Late-80s/early-90s rap: breakbeats, funk and jazz samples, scratches _Also: old school hip hop, oldschool rap, golden era._
- **East Coast hip-hop** (`east-coast-hip-hop` → Hip-Hop) — Gritty New York boom bap: dark piano loops, hard snares, dense lyricism _Also: east coast rap, new york rap._
- **G-funk** (`g-funk` → Hip-Hop, Funk) — West Coast funk-rap: whiny portamento synth leads, P-funk bass, laid-back swing _Also: west coast hip hop, west coast rap, gfunk._
- **Jazz rap** (`jazz-rap` → Hip-Hop, Jazz) — Mellow hip-hop over jazz samples: upright bass, muted trumpet, Rhodes _Also: jazz hop, jazzhop, conscious rap, abstract hip hop._
- **Emo rap** (`emo-rap` → Trap, Emo) — Sad, melodic rap over trap drums and lo-fi emo guitar loops _Also: sad rap, emo trap, soundcloud rap._
- **Cloud rap** (`cloud-rap` → Trap, Ambient) — Dreamy, reverb-drowned trap with ethereal pads and floating vocals _Also: cloud-rap._
- **Rage** (`rage-trap` → Trap, Hyperpop) — Hyperactive trap with blown-out, distorted supersaw leads and moshing energy _Also: rage beat, rage rap._
- **Plugg** (`plugg` → Trap, R&B) — Soft, twinkly trap: pluggy square-wave melodies, sparse 808s and airy pads _Also: pluggnb._
- **Trap soul** (`trap-soul` → R&B, Trap) — R&B vocals floating over minimal trap drums and moody minor chords _Also: trapsoul, trap&b, trap rnb._
- **Pop rap** (`pop-rap` → Hip-Hop, Pop) — Radio rap with sung pop hooks and bright production _Also: pop-rap._
- **Crunk** (`crunk` → Trap, Hip-Hop) — Dirty-south party rap: chanted hooks, synth stabs, booming 808s _Also: dirty south, snap music._
- **Memphis rap** (`memphis-rap` → Phonk, Hip-Hop) — Lo-fi, horror-tinged 90s Memphis tapes: cowbells, 808s and triplet flows _Also: memphis rap, horrorcore._
- **Chopped & screwed** (`chopped-and-screwed` → Hip-Hop) — Houston-style: slowed-down, pitched-down tracks with chopped, stuttering repeats _Also: chopped and screwed, screwed, screw music._
- **Latin trap** (`latin-trap` → Trap, Reggaetón) — Spanish-language trap: dark minor loops, 808s and reggaetón-flavoured hooks _Also: trap latino, urbano._
- **Afro trap** (`afro-trap` → Afrobeats, Trap) — French/UK rap over afrobeats-flavoured percussion and trap 808s _Also: afroswing, afro swing._
- **Hyphy** (`hyphy` → Hip-Hop) — Bay Area party rap: slapping, bouncing 808s, synth stabs and chants _Also: bay area rap._
- **New Orleans bounce** (`bounce` → Hip-Hop) — Call-and-response party rap on the Triggerman and Brown beats _Also: bounce music, new orleans bounce._
- **Desi hip-hop** (`desi-hip-hop` → Hip-Hop, Bollywood) — South Asian rap: dhol and tabla flavours, sampled Bollywood strings _Also: desi rap, gully rap, punjabi rap._
- **Nerdcore** (`nerdcore` → Hip-Hop, Chiptune) — Playful, wordy rap about games and geekdom over chiptune-flavoured beats

### R&B, soul & funk

- **Neo-soul** (`neo-soul` → Soul, R&B) — Organic, jazz-inflected soul: lazy swung grooves, Rhodes, extended chords, live bass _Also: neo soul, neosoul._
- **Quiet storm** (`quiet-storm` → R&B, Soul) — Late-night 80s slow jams: silky vocals, soft keys, sax and gentle grooves _Also: slow jam, slow jams._
- **New jack swing** (`new-jack-swing` → R&B, Hip-Hop) — Late-80s swung drum machines, gospel chords, synth stabs and dance-floor R&B _Also: swingbeat, new jack._
- **Contemporary R&B** (`contemporary-rnb` → R&B) — Modern R&B: crisp programmed drums, atmospheric keys, layered runs _Also: modern rnb, modern r&b._
- **Alternative R&B** (`alternative-rnb` → R&B, Ambient) — Moody, experimental R&B: hazy pads, sparse beats, falsetto and reverb _Also: alt r&b, alt-rnb, pbr&b._
- **Motown** (`motown` → Soul) — 60s Detroit soul: four-on-the-snare backbeat, tambourine, melodic bass and strings _Also: motown sound, detroit soul._
- **Northern soul** (`northern-soul` → Soul) — Uptempo, stomping soul for all-nighters: driving four-to-the-floor snare
- **Philly soul** (`philly-soul` → Soul, Disco) — Lush 70s Philadelphia soul: sweeping strings, horns, hi-hat-driven grooves _Also: philadelphia soul, sweet soul._
- **Southern soul** (`southern-soul-style` → Soul, Blues) — Gritty Memphis/Muscle Shoals soul: horn punches, organ, gospel fire _Also: stax, memphis soul, muscle shoals._
- **Psychedelic soul** (`psychedelic-soul` → Soul, Funk) — Late-60s soul with fuzz guitars, wah, long jams and political swagger
- **P-funk** (`p-funk` → Funk) — Parliament-style funk: squelchy synth bass, chanted hooks, cosmic weirdness _Also: pfunk, parliament funk._
- **Go-go** (`go-go` → Funk) — Washington DC funk: non-stop conga-driven swing beat and call-and-response _Also: gogo, go go._
- **Boogie** (`boogie-funk` → Funk, Disco) — Early-80s post-disco funk: synth bass, vocoders, slick drum machines _Also: post-disco, synth funk._
- **Funk rock** (`funk-rock` → Funk, Rock) — Slap bass and distorted guitar riffs, big drums and syncopated swagger _Also: funk metal._
- **Afrobeat (Fela)** (`afrobeat-fela` → Funk, Afrobeats) — Long, hypnotic Afro-funk jams: interlocking guitars, horn riffs, polyrhythmic percussion _Also: fela, afro-funk, afro funk._
- **Contemporary gospel** (`contemporary-gospel` → Gospel, R&B) — Modern gospel: R&B production, stacked choir, big key changes _Also: urban gospel._
- **Southern gospel** (`southern-gospel` → Gospel, Country) — Quartet harmonies over country-tinged piano and steady two-beat
- **Worship** (`worship` → Pop, Gospel) — Modern praise and worship: ambient guitars, swelling pads, anthemic congregational choruses _Also: praise and worship, ccm, christian contemporary._

### Jazz & blues

- **Bebop** (`bebop` → Jazz) — Fast, virtuosic small-group jazz: rhythm changes, dense ii–V lines, horn heads _Also: bop, hard bop._
- **Cool jazz** (`cool-jazz` → Jazz) — Relaxed, airy West Coast jazz with soft tones and gentle swing
- **Modal jazz** (`modal-jazz` → Jazz) — Long stretches on one mode: dorian vamps, quartal voicings, spacious solos _Also: modal vamp._
- **Smooth jazz** (`smooth-jazz` → Jazz, R&B) — Polished, radio-friendly jazz-pop: soprano sax, Rhodes, gentle backbeat _Also: smooth jazz._
- **Jazz fusion** (`jazz-fusion` → Jazz, Funk, Rock) — Electric jazz-rock: odd meters, virtuoso solos, synths and slap bass _Also: fusion, jazz rock._
- **Big band swing** (`big-band` → Jazz) — Swing-era orchestra: riffing saxes and brass sections, walking bass, shout choruses _Also: swing music, swing era, big band._
- **Latin jazz** (`latin-jazz` → Jazz, Salsa) — Jazz harmony over Afro-Cuban clave grooves, congas and montunos _Also: afro-cuban jazz._
- **Gypsy jazz** (`gypsy-jazz` → Jazz) — Hot-club swing: driving acoustic "la pompe" rhythm guitar, violin and virtuoso leads _Also: jazz manouche, manouche, hot club._
- **Acid jazz** (`acid-jazz` → Jazz, Funk) — Groovy jazz-funk with breakbeats, Hammond organ and horns _Also: jazz funk, jazz-funk._
- **Free jazz** (`free-jazz` → Jazz) — Unbound improvisation: dissonance, shifting time, collective blowing _Also: avant-garde jazz._
- **Vocal jazz** (`vocal-jazz` → Jazz) — Standards sung by a crooner over piano trio: ballads and medium swing _Also: jazz standards, jazz vocals._
- **Dixieland** (`dixieland` → Jazz) — New Orleans trad jazz: two-beat feel, collective polyphony of trumpet, clarinet and trombone _Also: new orleans jazz, trad jazz, second line._
- **Ragtime** (`ragtime` → Jazz) — Syncopated stride piano: oom-pah left hand, ragged right-hand melodies _Also: stride, stride piano._
- **Delta blues** (`delta-blues` → Blues, Folk) — Raw acoustic slide guitar and voice, free-flowing time, deep moans _Also: country blues, acoustic blues._
- **Chicago blues** (`chicago-blues` → Blues) — Electric band blues: amplified harmonica, piano, shuffling rhythm section _Also: electric blues._
- **Jump blues** (`jump-blues` → Blues, Jazz) — Uptempo jumping R&B with honking sax, horn riffs and boogie bass
- **Boogie-woogie** (`boogie-woogie` → Blues, Jazz) — Rolling eighth-note piano bass figures under bluesy right-hand riffs _Also: boogie woogie._
- **Desert blues** (`desert-blues` → Blues, Afrobeats) — Tuareg guitar trance: hypnotic modal riffs, handclaps and rolling grooves _Also: tuareg, assouf._
- **Ethio-jazz** (`ethio-jazz` → Jazz, Funk) — Ethiopian pentatonic modes over jazz-funk grooves with vibraphone and horns _Also: ethiojazz, ethiopian jazz._

### Folk, country & roots

- **Americana** (`americana` → Folk, Country) — Roots-rock storytelling: acoustic and electric guitars, pedal steel, harmonica, warm room _Also: roots rock, roots music._
- **Outlaw country** (`outlaw-country` → Country) — 70s rebel country: twangy Telecasters, loose shuffles, baritone swagger _Also: outlaw._
- **Bro-country** (`bro-country` → Country, Pop) — 2010s arena country: hip-hop drum loops, big guitars, party hooks _Also: bro country, country rap, hick hop._
- **Country pop** (`country-pop` → Country, Pop) — Glossy crossover country: pop hooks, acoustic strums and big choruses _Also: pop country._
- **Honky-tonk** (`honky-tonk` → Country) — Barroom country: two-step shuffle, crying fiddle and pedal steel, piano rolls _Also: honky tonk, two-step, texas two step._
- **Western swing** (`western-swing` → Country, Jazz) — Swinging country dance band: fiddles, steel guitar and jazz chords
- **Cowboy / western** (`cowboy` → Country, Folk) — Wide-open western ballads: galloping rhythm, campfire guitar, lonesome whistle _Also: western, country western._
- **Folk rock** (`folk-rock` → Folk, Rock) — Folk songs with an electric band: jangly guitars, harmonies, steady backbeat
- **Folk-pop** (`folk-pop` → Folk, Pop) — Bright acoustic pop with stomps, claps and singalong "hey"s _Also: stomp and holler._
- **Neofolk** (`neofolk` → Folk) — Dark, martial acoustic folk with drones and ritual percussion _Also: dark folk._
- **Appalachian folk** (`appalachian-folk` → Folk, Bluegrass) — Old mountain ballads: modal melodies, banjo and fiddle, lonesome harmony _Also: old-time, old time, mountain music._
- **Newgrass** (`newgrass` → Bluegrass) — Progressive bluegrass: jazz and rock harmony, extended jams on acoustic strings _Also: progressive bluegrass._
- **Zydeco** (`zydeco` → Folk, Blues) — Louisiana Creole dance music: accordion, rubboard and a syncopated two-step _Also: cajun._
- **Tejano / norteño** (`tejano` → Cumbia, Country) — Texas-Mexican polka-cumbia: button accordion, bajo sexto, bouncy two-beat _Also: norteño, norteno, tex-mex, regional mexican._
- **Polka** (`polka` → Folk) — Oom-pah two-beat dance: accordion, tuba-like bass on 1 and 3, chords on the off-beats _Also: oom-pah, oompah._
- **Sea shanty** (`sea-shanty` → Folk, Celtic) — Call-and-response work songs: stomping 6/8, gang choruses, squeezebox _Also: shanty, sea shanties, shanties._
- **Nordic folk** (`nordic-folk` → Folk, Celtic) — Scandinavian folk: droning fiddles, minor modes, ritual drums and kulning _Also: scandinavian folk, viking folk._
- **Chanson** (`chanson` → Singer-Songwriter, Folk) — French cabaret song: accordion waltzes, wry lyrics, intimate piano _Also: french chanson, cabaret, musette._
- **Fado** (`fado` → Singer-Songwriter, Flamenco) — Portuguese saudade: mournful voice over Portuguese guitar and nylon guitar

### Latin

- **Bachata** (`bachata` → Latin Pop, Cumbia) — Dominican romance: chiming requinto guitar arpeggios, bongó and güira, syncopated bass
- **Merengue** (`merengue` → Cumbia, Salsa) — Fast Dominican two-beat: tambora, güira and saxophone/accordion riffs
- **Mambo** (`mambo` → Salsa) — 1950s big-band mambo: brass riffs, piano montuno and syncopated horn hits
- **Cha-cha-chá** (`cha-cha-cha` → Salsa) — Elegant mid-tempo Cuban dance: güiro on the beats, "one-two-cha-cha-cha" bass _Also: cha cha, chachacha, charanga._
- **Bolero** (`bolero` → Latin Pop, Bossa Nova) — Slow Latin romance in 4/4: soft guitars, strings, gentle bongó

- **Forró** (`forro` → Samba, Cumbia) — Northeast Brazilian dance music: accordion, zabumba drum and triangle _Also: forró, baião._

- **Tango** (`tango` → Flamenco, Orchestral) — Argentine tango: bandoneon, marcato four-beat, dramatic minor harmony and string staccatos _Also: tango nuevo, argentine tango._
- **Vallenato** (`vallenato` → Cumbia) — Colombian accordion music: caja, guacharaca and storytelling vocals
- **Mariachi** (`mariachi` → Latin Pop, Folk) — Mexican mariachi: trumpets, violins, vihuela and guitarrón in 3/4 and 6/8 _Also: ranchera, son jarocho._

### Caribbean

### World & traditional

### Classical & cinematic

- **Baroque** (`baroque` → Orchestral) — Bach-era counterpoint: busy harmonic rhythm, sequences, walking continuo bass _Also: baroque period, bach._
- **Romantic era** (`romantic-era` → Orchestral) — 19th-century lyricism: sweeping strings, chromatic harmony, big dynamics _Also: romantic period, late romantic._

- **Opera** (`opera` → Orchestral, Musical Theatre) — Operatic aria: soaring classical voice, orchestra, dramatic recitative and climaxes _Also: aria._

- **Marching band** (`marching-band` → Orchestral) — Brass and drumline in 2/4: snare cadences, sousaphone and fanfares _Also: drumline, military march._

## Production tags

- **Lo-fi** (`lo-fi`) — Dusty, laid-back and slightly behind the beat _Also: lofi, lo fi._
- **Tape-saturated** (`tape-saturated`) — Warm analog tape: rounded transients, gentle wow and flutter _Also: tape, analog tape, tape saturation._
- **Live room** (`live-room`) — A band playing together in a room: looser timing, natural ambience _Also: live band, live recording, room sound._
- **Polished** (`polished`) — Radio-ready gloss: tight edits, quantized, bright and loud _Also: glossy, radio-ready, slick._
- **Bedroom production** (`bedroom`) — Made at home: soft, a little rough, intimate and quiet _Also: home recorded, diy._
- **Wall of sound** (`wall-of-sound`) — Dense, layered, echo-drenched production: everything doubled
- **Minimal** (`minimal`) — Less is more: few elements, lots of space _Also: minimalist, sparse, stripped-back, stripped back._
- **Maximal** (`maximal`) — More is more: layered, busy, everything at once _Also: maximalist, huge production._

- **Orchestral hybrid** (`orchestral-hybrid`) — Synths and orchestra layered: pulses under strings and brass _Also: orchestral hybrid._

- **Distorted** (`distorted`) — Saturated and overdriven: crushed drums, fuzz, clipping _Also: overdriven, saturated, blown out, fuzzy._
- **Dry** (`dry`) — Close and dead: almost no reverb, upfront and present _Also: close-miked, dead room, upfront._
- **Reverb-drenched** (`reverb-drenched`) — Huge spaces: long tails, washes, cathedral ambience _Also: washed out, cavernous, drenched in reverb, spacious._
- **Vinyl** (`vinyl`) — Record-crackle texture and a gentle, sample-like warmth _Also: vinyl crackle, record crackle._
- **Glitchy** (`glitch`) — Stutters, buffer edits and digital artifacts _Also: glitchy, stutter._

- **Raw** (`raw`) — Unpolished first-take energy: loose, live, unprocessed _Also: unpolished, first take._
- **Brushed drums** (`brushed-drums`) — Drums played with brushes: soft swishing snare, feathered kick, no crashing _Also: brushes, brushed, brush kit._

## Rhythm and meter tags

### Rhythm & meter

- **Half-time** (`half-time`) — Snare on 3: heavier, slower-feeling groove at the same tempo _Also: halftime, half time._

- **Straight feel** (`straight`) — Straight, even eighths: no swing _Also: straight eighths, even eighths._

- **7/8 time** (`seven-eight`) — Seven eighths (2+2+3): limping, propulsive _Also: seven eight, in seven._

- **12/8 feel** (`twelve-eight`) — Slow-blues/soul-ballad triplet feel _Also: 12/8, twelve eight._
